completion_data.completion_summary: Phase 2 of 5: the proof-mode record now states the linearity edge and the proposed induction rule in M4, the Minus deduction theorem's move in M9a, BimodalLib outside the default targets in M18, the views pair and layer in M16, and the order M17, M0, M16, with the adoption question restated and still open.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic proof-mode milestone order of M16 and M17
sapience_notes.value: records/proof-mode.md orders logical rewriting (M17), then the operator-family layout (M0), then the views tier (M16). M17 carries no sequencing dependency on M16; M0 already runs after open contributions are merged or declined, so no new filed edge is needed. M16 takes over the view rows M17 contributes. Rejected: building M16 first and rebasing M17 onto it (drops M16's edge on M0 and holds a contribution on unscheduled work), and merging M17 with lrewrite still handling formula equalities (one tactic name serving two tiers).

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic linearity case split and Until/Since induction
sapience_notes.value: The linearity case-split record is a sequencing-only predecessor of every part of the Until/Since record, the induction rule included: the pure rule sits under FormalSystem/Theorems/ProofMode/ at layer 2 and cannot import a tactic, so it takes linearity as a theorem (Axiom.linear_until, Theorems/LinearityDerived.lean). This holds whatever the rule's formula is.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic proposed Until induction rule generalizing forwardInvariantRule
sapience_notes.value: Proposed, not derived or machine-checked: at ZTime, with strict operators and X phi := untl bot phi, |- (X(e or (g and C)) -> C) -> G(X(e or (g and C)) -> C) -> (g U e -> C), with the Since mirror by time reflection. Setting g := top, e := not A, C := not A recovers forwardInvariantRule up to argument order. Backward induction (futureBackwardInduction) is a different rule and forwardInvariantRule is not an instance of it.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic Minus proof-mode instance placement
sapience_notes.value: MinusDeduction.lean moves from FormalSystem/Metalogic/Conservativity/ (layer 3) to FormalSystem/Theorems/, with MinusTemporalDerived.lean if needed, so the Minus pure-rule module sits under FormalSystem/Theorems/ProofMode/ like TM and TM-plus; M9a carries out the move. Both files import layer 0 only and all importers are at layer 3. Rejected: instance at layer 3 (scheme exception), and moving into MinusLanguage/ (the per-file rule would keep it at layer 3).

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic BimodalLib build target
sapience_notes.value: BimodalLib is a Lake library outside defaultTargets, built by explicit target and its own --wfail CI step as BimodalTools is, with an import-direction check that FormalSystem never imports it. A default target was rejected because CI catches the same drift and a plain lake build is stated to compile the published library only.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic proof-mode adoption, meaning of default (M12)
sapience_notes.value: Still open and awaiting the user's ruling. Options: A new Examples and case-study modules in the mode; B every new derived theorem registered in BimodalLib with a proof-mode script or a recorded failure class; C optional outside sweeps. Recommendation: B as the rule, A for Examples and case studies, Theorems/ exempt by layering, all contingent on a GO at gate one. M12's done-when already excludes C.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic M17 rewriting comparison depends on gate one's sweep
sapience_notes.value: M17's done-when clause 'at least one library entry in a sweep is shorter' is met by a second run of the gate-one selection with lrewrite and lsimp permitted, reported apart from the gate's verdict. The tactics have no hard dependency, but that comparison can only run once M3's sweep exists, so M17 cannot fully close before M3 even though it is merged before M0.
